$comment: NL Design System theme -> Nextcloud token set: the whole mapping, as data.
Loaded by BOTH runtimes -- js/lib/tokenConverter.js (CLI, vitest, browser) and
lib/Service/TokenSetConverterService.php (the admin upload and paste path) -- so the two
cannot drift. The SHA-256 of this file is written into every converted token set's
provenance block, which is how a set generated by an older table is spotted without
running anything. See openspec/changes/nlds-theme-converter/design.md decision 1.
ORDER MATTERS TWICE. `never` is walked BEFORE `rules`, so a source token can only be
applied if it survived the policy; and within a rule, `sources` is a priority list where
the first one the input declares wins.
`{p}` is the brand prefix, which is the token set's slug (openwoo, nijmegen, custom-acme).
NOT IN THIS TABLE, deliberately: the --nldesign-component-* bridge names. The converted
file emits the theme's own --utrecht-* / --ams-* / --denhaag-* declarations verbatim in its
component section, and css/utrecht-bridge.css already maps those onto --nldesign-component-*.
A hand-authored set such as css/tokens/openwoo.css has to declare the bridge names itself
because it carries no component section; converter output never does.
ALWAYS derived from the primary, never taken from a token. These are Nextcloud's
light TINTS of the element colour (hover backgrounds for primary-ish controls), so
they only make sense as a wash of the brand colour.
--utrecht-button-secondary-action-hover-background-color used to be the source here
and it is the wrong role: a theme whose secondary button is outlined sets that to
WHITE (OpenWOO does), which handed Nextcloud #ffffff for both tints and made every
primary hover state disappear. Compare css/tokens/cunningham.css, which pairs
#1a509f with #eaf1fb / #d5e4f7 -- a 10% and a 20% wash, which is what these weights
reproduce.
nav-background is resolved EARLY, before every rule that measures contrast against it.
Rules are walked in array order and a guard can only see targets already resolved, so
when this sat further down, `-text-muted` and `-border-dark` fell back to assuming a
white page and `-header-border-bottom`'s sameColor test could never fire.
GEOMETRY IS NEXTCLOUD'S, COLOUR IS THE BRAND'S. A converted set is a RESKIN:
Nextcloud with the design system's colours, not Nextcloud rebuilt to the design
system's shapes. So the radius scale is Nextcloud 32's own (8 / 4 / 8 / 28 / 100)
and the theme's control radius is NOT a source for it.
This was learned the hard way twice. Taking the brand's control radius squares off
the app shell, navigation entries, search field, buttons and modals wherever a
brand is near-square -- OpenWOO's 3px and Zwolle's 2px both do it, and Cunningham's
flat 4px did it too, which is why css/tokens/cunningham.css pins this same scale by
hand and documents why. The brand's own radius stays available to NL Design System
components through the untouched --utrecht-* component layer.
Literals, not var() references: css/systems/nldesign/overrides.css maps Nextcloud's
scale FROM these tokens, so referencing it back would be a cycle.
Table headers are Nextcloud's too: the shared NLDS theme paints every `th` with the
design system's table-header colour, where a stock Files list shows muted labels on
no background. Same three literals css/tokens/cunningham.css sets by hand.
THE LOGO IS AN ASSET, NOT A COLOUR, so it cannot be a `rules[]` entry: those map one
declaration to another declaration, and this one has to leave the stylesheet entirely.
Nextcloud's core theming takes a logo as a FILE (ImageManager::updateImage), and the
theming-sync spec requires `theming.logo` to be a path under img/logos/ that exists on
disk — a base64 data URI can never satisfy that, so a converted theme could never
update the Nextcloud logo however complete its colours were.
An NL Design System theme ships its wordmark inline: `--conduction-logo-header-
background-image: url("data:image/svg+xml;base64,…")` is how @conduction/theme carries
OpenWOO's. The converter decodes that payload, writes it as img/logos/<asset>.<ext>,
points --nldesign-logo-url at the written file and records the path in the manifest, so
the same artwork drives the app header AND Nextcloud's own logo slot. It also keeps the
emitted token set small: the alternative is ~40 KB of base64 in a file served to every
anonymous visitor on the login page.
`sources` is walked in order and the first hit wins, exactly like a rule's sources;
`roles` then catches a theme whose vendor prefix this app has never seen. Every other
declaration carrying the same payload is rewritten to var(--nldesign-logo-url) — the
shape css/tokens/opencatalogi.css already uses for its three conduction logo slots.

reasons.layout-fixed-by-nextcloud: Page width and paddings were not applied. Nextcloud uses a fluid, full-width layout; a fixed page width would break the app grid and the sidebar.
reasons.typography-scale-locked: Font sizes and line heights were not applied. Nextcloud sizes text from its own 15px baseline so icons, inputs and rows stay aligned; use the browser zoom or Nextcloud's accessibility settings instead.
reasons.clickable-area-locked: Button and input paddings were not applied. Nextcloud keeps a 34px/44px minimum clickable area for WCAG 2.5.8.
reasons.spacing-not-consumed: Spacing tokens were kept in the file for NL Design System components but Nextcloud's own components do not read them.
reasons.routed-to-core-theming: The page background was applied through Nextcloud's theming settings (login page and plain background), not as the content background, so dark mode keeps working.
reasons.derived-by-nextcloud: This value is calculated by Nextcloud from the primary colour (element colour, light tints, contrast text) and cannot be set directly.
reasons.radius-scale-derived: Corner radii were derived from the theme's button and textbox radius; pill and round shapes are fixed.
reasons.geometry-kept-nextcloud: Shapes and sizes stay Nextcloud's: a token set is a reskin, so it carries the design system's COLOURS and leaves corner radii, border widths and table-header styling to Nextcloud. The theme's own values are kept in the file for NL Design System components.
reasons.font-not-bundled: The theme's font is referenced but not installed. Upload it under Custom fonts or the next font in the stack is used.
reasons.contrast-separator-added: A 1px header border was added because the theme's header and content are both the same colour.
reasons.contrast-adjusted: The colour was darkened to reach WCAG AA 4.5:1 against its text colour. The original is shown for reference.
reasons.kept-for-nlds-components: Kept in the token set for NL Design System components used by Conduction apps; Nextcloud itself does not have this component.
reasons.external-url-blocked: A value pointed to an external host and was removed; Thematiq only serves local assets.
reasons.unmapped: No Nextcloud equivalent was found. Listed so it can be added to the mapping table.
reasons.palette-reprefixed: A raw palette step was declared under the app's own vocabulary and was moved to the brand prefix, where the semantic layer can read it.
reasons.unresolved-var: The value referenced a variable the theme does not define, so it was left out: a token set is also served on the login page and in e-mails, where that variable does not exist.
reasons.at-rule-not-converted: Declarations inside a media query or other at-rule were not converted; a token set is one flat block of values.
reasons.kept-existing-value: The token set already declared this value, so it was kept; re-conversion only fills gaps.
reasons.derived-from-header: Derived from the theme's own header colour rather than taken from a token.
reasons.derived-from-brand: The theme does not declare this role, so the value was derived from the theme's own colours (a darkened or mixed brand colour, or a step from its grey ramp).
reasons.nextcloud-default-used: The theme declares nothing for this role and nothing could be derived from it, so Nextcloud's own default was used.
reasons.logo-extracted: The theme's logo was decoded out of its token and stored as an image file, so it can drive both the app header and Nextcloud's own logo, name and e-mail branding.
reasons.logo-format-unsupported: The theme's logo could not be stored as an image: it is not an inline SVG, PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, or it is larger than the 256 KB limit. Upload a logo under Nextcloud's own theming settings instead.
